messages:
maya: Hey — during HF->Redwood conversion of the new quantized finetune I’m seeing streaming outputs terminate early, then emit another EOS a few tokens later. Repro on local serve with `--stream` and `--quantize=4bit`.
ryan: Can you paste the model `config.json` and tokenizer special tokens? sounds like `eos_token_id` mismatch or duplicate special tokens.
maya: config snippet:
```
"eos_token_id": 2,
"pad_token_id": 1,
"bos_token_id": 0,
"special_tokens_map": {"eos_token": "</s>", "additional_special_tokens": ["<|end|>"]}
```
maya: tokenizer vocab seems to map `</s>` -> 2 and `<|end|>` -> 2 as well (two entries pointed to same id). not sure how HF ended up with that mapping.
jorge: interesting. If both special tokens map to id 2 the runtime may emit EOS once then later another token gets decoded to the same id and triggers stop sequence handling twice. streaming layer is supposed to dedupe contiguous EOS but we only dedupe identical consecutive token ids, not non-contiguous duplicates.
emma: repro idea: prompt that intentionally causes insertion between the two EOS tokens (e.g., trailing punctuation) — if the model emits `</s>` then a punctuation token then `<|end|>` (same id) the streaming code will see token ids: [2, 8, 2] and think there are two EOS occurrences separated by non-EOS, so it will terminate on the first 2 and then still send the later 2 as a normal token that decodes to `</s>` which triggers the client-side stop sequence logic again.
ryan: do we have a streaming test that covers duplicate-mapped-special-tokens? think we assumed special tokens are unique ids.
maya: not for this exact case. I can craft a minimal repro using the HF tokenizer and a tiny LM that was quantized — will attach logs.
deploy-bot: deploy status: test model v0.4.2-quant queued -> started on devpool-2 (g4dn). Logs: `stream:token: 2 -> decoded: </s>` \n `stream:token: 244 -> decoded: .` \n `stream:token: 2 -> decoded: </s>`
jorge: quick fix options:
- normalise tokenizer on conversion: collapse duplicate special tokens and ensure unique ids
- change streaming code to track already-emitted special token ids for the lifetime of a response (not only contiguous dedupe)
- update chat-template/stopseq matching to operate on decoded strings rather than raw tokens and ignore repeated decoded stop strings once emitted
emma: last option might be brittle for high-throughput path due to decoding cost per token. we could special-case only stop strings that are short and common.
maya: created issue and PR draft: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/issue/1234 — includes minimal repro and patched conversion script to prefer the first-occurring special token id.
ryan: if conversion script prefers first special token id it might change behavior for downstream evals. please add a changelog and add a conversion flag `--preserve-duplicates` to opt out.
maya: will do. also adding an eval that runs short streaming prompts and asserts that we only emit one stop event per logical stop string. test will include quantized runs.
jorge: also check `chat_templates` loader: some templates supply `stop_sequences: ["\n\n", "</s>"]` and we match against decoded substrings — if decoded stream contains `</s>` twice but we already triggered stop we should suppress further streaming events and just close the connection. sounds like a server-side bug to me.
maya: agreed. for the immediate customer report I’ll roll the conversion fix and add server dedupe guard. thanks all :thumbsup:
ryan: thanks — please add the failing prompt to the regression suite so we don't regress when we change quant kernels.
maya: already added. linking once PR lands.
